title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, and Onboarding
author: Ava Martinez
summary: A consolidated handbook entry covering what it's like to work at Redwood, role and career ladder guidance for ICs and managers, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and practical internal tools setup and first-week checklist.
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page is the canonical People Ops handbook entry for new and existing employees who want a single reference for role expectations, promotion criteria, benefits, the hiring and onboarding lifecycle, and the set of internal tools engineers and non-engineers commonly use. Keep this page as the first-stop guide; link to team-specific pages for details.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & values

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on reliable, cost‑effective LLM inference. Our culture emphasizes ownership, engineering craftsmanship, customer empathy, and psychological safety. Core behaviors we expect:
- Ship high-quality, observable systems (SLO-driven design).
- Prioritize clarity: clear docs, runbooks, and PR descriptions.
- Collaborate cross-functionally: product, security, SRE, and customers.
- Continuous learning: postmortems, dojos, and external conference participation.

Expectations by tenure:
- New joiners (0–3 months): learn product, complete onboarding checklist, run a small internal demo.
- Contributors (3–12 months): own a medium scope project, participate in on-call rotations if applicable.
- Leaders (>12 months): drive cross-team initiatives and mentorship.

2) Roles & career ladders

This section summarizes the company career ladders for individual contributors (IC) and managers (EM). Full ladder matrices and leveling rubrics are maintained in People Ops -> Career Ladders (link below). The expectations below are intentionally high-level and role-agnostic.

IC ladder (example levels):
- IC1 (Junior Engineer): demonstrates core engineering fundamentals, completes tasks with guidance.
- IC2 (Engineer): owns end-to-end features, writes reliable tests and runbooks.
- IC3 (Senior Engineer): leads design for medium systems, mentors others, influences roadmap.
- IC4 (Staff Engineer): drives architecture across multiple teams, defines standards and performance targets.
- IC5 (Principal/Distinguished): thought leadership, long-term platform direction, external representation.

Manager ladder (example levels):
- M1 (Manager): people manager for a small team (3–8), responsible for delivery and growth.
- M2 (Senior Manager): multiple teams or larger scope, cross-team program ownership.
- M3 (Director+): org-level leadership, strategic planning, and cross-functional partnerships.

Promotion criteria (common signals):
- Delivering consistent impact: measurable project outcomes tied to customer or operational metrics.
- Scope expansion: influence beyond immediate team and ownership of cross-team initiatives.
- Coaching & hiring: documented mentorship and participation in recruiting/hiring.
- Technical depth or management effectiveness: depending on ladder.

Promotion process (high-level):
1. Candidate or manager triggers promotion review via People Ops form.
2. Manager prepares evidence: PRs, project summaries, metrics, 360 feedback.
3. Calibration panel: cross-functional reviewers assess against rubric.
4. Outcome communicated; career plan updated.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Core benefits (US primary example; EU/APAC variants available — see Benefits Hub):
- Health: medical, dental, vision plans with Redwood covering a significant portion of premiums.
- Retirement: 401(k) with employer match (US).
- Equity: annual grants for full-time employees; vesting schedule in offer letter.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO baseline (pro-rated first year), 10 company holidays + Winter Close (Dec 24–Jan 1).
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (paid).
- Family support: fertility and adoption assistance stipend.
- Learning & travel: $2,000 annual learning stipend and conference/travel allowance.
- Wellness: monthly wellness stipend and EAP.

Perks and reimbursements:
- Home office stipend (one-time), monthly internet subsidy.
- Commuter benefits where applicable; public transit pass reimbursement.
- Referral bonus program and spot recognition awards.

Benefits admin examples (table):
| Benefit | Owner | Where to enroll | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Health insurance | People Ops | Benefits Portal (WorkBright) | Open enrollment Nov each year |
| 401(k) | Finance/People Ops | Payroll provider | Employer match up to 4% |
| Equity | Finance | Equity Portal | Grants executed at hire/refresh cycles |

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

High-level hiring flow (standard IC role):
1. Requisition opened by hiring manager in Greenhouse with scorecard.
2. Sourcing & screening (Recruiter) — phone screen + take-home exercise (if applicable).
3. Interview loop: Hiring Manager, Peer, Cross-functional partner (SRE/Infra), Manager level, Hiring Committee.
4. Offer: compensation calibrated with People Ops and Finance; offer letter issued in DocuSign.
5. Background check and reference checks as permitted by region.
6. Start date & preboarding.

Interview timeline targets:
- Screen to onsite loop: median 14 days.
- Offer after loop: within 48–72 hours of final interview.

Preboarding checklist (recruiter + new hire):
- Confirm start date, send preboarding packet, employment forms, and benefits enrollment links.
- Create accounts: GitHub, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, Jira, Okta MFA enrollment.
- Schedule first-week onboarding meetings: People Ops orientation, IT setup, team orientation, buddy pairing.

First-week onboarding (numbered schedule):
1. Day 0 (pre-start): confirm equipment shipping and access.
2. Day 1: People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, code of conduct), lunch with manager and buddy.
3. Day 2: Security & compliance training, MFA & KMS overview, SSO walkthrough.
4. Day 3: Development environment setup, repo access, first small task assigned.
5. Day 4: Product deep-dive and roadmap session.
6. Day 5: Team demo, onboarding retro, 30/60/90 day plan kickoff.

5) Internal tools & developer environment guide

Accounts and access (owners):
- Identity: Okta (IT/security). Enroll MFA within 24 hours of account creation.
- Code: GitHub (eng-developer-experience) — request org membership via onboarding ticket.
- Tickets & planning: Jira (eng-platform).
- Docs: Confluence (company-handbook + team spaces).
- Communication: Slack (All Company channels + team channels).
- Cloud console(s): AWS account (eng-infra) and GCP where applicable. Dedicated customers may have separate VPCs and RBAC profiles.

Developer local setup (example commands)
1. Install dev tooling (macOS):
   - brew install docker git golang node
2. Clone repos and bootstrap:
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/platform.git
   - cd platform && make bootstrap
3. Start local services (devctl is our helper tool):
   - devctl up --env local
   - devctl migrate-db
4. Run unit tests:
   - make test

Notes: If you see long cold-start times for local models, ensure your local docker resources are >= 8GB RAM and 4 CPUs. For GPU development, contact eng-infra for dev GPU allocation.

Access & security (quick checklist):
- Enroll in Okta MFA and YubiKey if you have one.
- Complete Security Basics training within first week.
- Never check secrets into Git; use Secrets Manager (internal).

Common support flows (who to contact):
- Access requests: it-support@redwood.com (IT queue).
- GitHub or repo access: eng-developer-experience@redwood.com.
- Local dev or infra issues: #eng-infra on Slack and the infra runbooks page.

6) First 90 days & career development

30/60/90 framework (manager + new hire):
- 30-day: learn systems, complete onboarding checklist, deliver first small milestone.
- 60-day: own a feature end-to-end, participate in code reviews, begin mentoring.
- 90-day: measurable impact, draft growth plan and potential next-scope areas.

Learning & development offerings:
- Bi-weekly dojos, recorded and available on Confluence.
- Mentorship program: match within 2–4 weeks of start.
- Manager 1:1 cadence: weekly for first 12 weeks.

7) On-call, incident response & escalation

If your team is on-call, expect to:
- Attend on-call handoff and read the team runbook before your first shift.
- Respond to pages within 2 minutes for P0/P1 pages (SLO target).
- Triage, mitigate, and escalate by severity: follow the Incident Playbook (link).

Escalation matrix (short):
- P0 (service down): pager -> primary on-call -> secondary on-call -> SRE lead -> Eng Director.
- P1 (degraded): pager -> primary on-call -> owning team -> SRE/infra.

8) Policies and compliance highlights

- Data residency: follow Security & Compliance data-residency guidance for customer data.
- Audit logging: enable in services you manage per checklist; retention aligned to compliance team requirements.
- Acceptable use & code of conduct: mandatory review and acknowledgement during onboarding.

9) FAQ and common issues

Q: How do I request time off?
A: Submit PTO via the HR portal; discuss extended leaves with your manager and People Ops.

Q: Who approves learning stipend spending?
A: Manager approves; People Ops reimburses after receipts and completion documentation.

Q: Where are team-specific playbooks?
A: Confluence -> team space -> runbooks. If missing, open a ticket with eng-platform.
